sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
sources.authority_reason: The original authors define soft-target distillation and the hard/soft objective.
sources.inspection_note: pp.2-3, sections 1-2; p.3 equation (1); p.4 section 3. Read the original PDF text through section 3. Distillation uses the same high temperature on teacher/student, combines soft-target and hard-label cross entropy, and multiplies the soft gradients by T squared. Section 3 compares small architecture with ordinary training; none of this promises universal improvement. sources.details: For fixed teacher p and student q on the same candidate identities, KL(p||q)=sum_i p_i(log p_i-log q_i)=CE(p,q)-H(p). H(p) is independent of student parameters, so soft CE and forward KL have the same student gradient. With p=(0.8,0.2), q=(0.5,0.5), the hand calculation is 0.8 ln(1.6)+0.2 ln(0.4)=0.192744757; CE=ln2=0.693147181 and H=0.500402424. This is algebra/hand calculation, distinct from executed prerequisite outputs rounded to 0.1927. Comparing two equal-architecture, identical-init/data/update branches holds parameter count fixed; shrinking alone cannot be attributed to changing teacher loss. Prompt shape=square and pitch=high with joint? gives literal gold square,high; this derives a target and does not predict any learned model output. For a 16 by 16 image, patch side 4 gives (16/4)^2=16 image positions and side 8 gives 4; no end-to-end speed ratio follows.
